# Therapeutic Goods (Permissible Ingredients) Determination (No. 2) 2026

made under subsection 26BB(1) of the

Therapeutic Goods Act 1989

**Compilation No. 1**

**Compilation date:** 17 September 2026

**Includes amendments:** F2026L01211

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *Therapeutic Goods (Permissible Ingredients) Determination (No. 2) 2026* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 17 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

###### 1 Name

This instrument is the *Therapeutic Goods (Permissible Ingredients) Determination (No. 2) 2026*.

###### 3 Authority

This instrument is made under subsection 26BB(1) of the *Therapeutic Goods Act 1989*.

###### 4 Interpretation

Note: A number of expressions used in this instrument are defined in subsection 3(1) of the Act, including the following:

(a) British Pharmacopoeia;

(b) European Pharmacopoeia;

(c) medicine;

(d) Register;

(e) United States Pharmacopeia-National Formulary.

(1) In this instrument:

***Act*** means the *Therapeutic Goods Act 1989*.

***active ingredient***, or ***A***, for a medicine, has the same meaning as in the Regulations.

***code tables*** means the tables accessed via the *Code Tables* item in the *Public TGA Information* menu in TGA eBusiness Services.

***excipient*** or ***E***, for a medicine, means an ingredient that is not an active ingredient or a homoeopathic preparation ingredient.

Note: An excipient includes an ingredient that provides flavour, fragrance or colour to the medicine.

***homoeopathic preparation*** has the same meaning as in the Regulations.

***homoeopathic preparation ingredient*** or ***H***, means an ingredient that is a constituent of a homoeopathic preparation.

***Regulations*** means the *Therapeutic Goods Regulations 1990*.

***TGA eBusiness Services*** means TGA eBusiness Services on the Therapeutic Goods Administration website, which may be accessed on the internet at www.ebs.tga.gov.au.

***Therapeutic Goods Administration*** has the same meaning as in the Regulations.

(2) To avoid doubt, the terms set out in closed brackets in column 4 of the table in Schedule 1, which are associated with warning statements in relation to particular ingredients, are:

(a) terms from the code tables under the heading *Product Warning*; and

(b) not required to be reproduced in a warning statement on the label of a medicine.

Note: Examples of these terms include the following:

(a) (ARGIN1);

(b) (CHILD3);

(c) (GLUTEN);

(d) (PEANUT);

(e) (PREGNT).

###### 5 Permissible ingredients

The ingredients specified in column 2 of the table in Schedule 1 are specified for the purposes of paragraph 26BB(1)(a) of the Act.

###### 6 Requirements in relation to permissible ingredients being contained in medicine

For an ingredient mentioned in column 2 of an item in the table in Schedule 1, the following requirements are specified for the purposes of paragraph 26BB(1)(b) of the Act:

(a) the ingredient must only be used in a medicine for a purpose specified in relation to the ingredient in column 3 of that item; and

(b) subject to section 6A, the ingredient must comply with the requirements specified in relation to the ingredient in column 4 of that item; and

(c) if the ingredient is derived from animal originthe safety of the ingredient must have been assessed against, and comply with, the principles and requirements in the European Pharmacopoeia general monograph 1483 *Products with risk of transmitting agents of animal spongiform encephalopathies*, including General Text 5.2.8: *Minimising the risk of transmitting animal spongiform encephalopathy agents via human and veterinary medicinal products.*

###### 6A Requirements relating to warning statements on labels

Where more than one ingredient in a medicine (the ***relevant ingredients***) must comply with a requirement, specified in column 4 of the table in Schedule 1 in relation to the ingredient, that a warning statement must be stated on the medicine label (the ***specified warning statement***) in the form of either:

(a) “In [rare/very rare] cases, [ingredient] may harm the liver. Stop use and see a doctor if you have yellowing skin/eyes or unusual: fatigue, nausea, appetite loss, abdominal pain, dark urine or itching”; or

(b) “In [rare/very rare] cases, [ingredient] may harm the liver. Stop use and see a doctor if you have yellowing skin/eyes or unusual: fatigue, nausea, appetite loss, abdominal pain or dark urine”;

the warning statement may be stated only once on the label of the medicine (the ***combined warning statement***), provided that:

(c) the combined warning statement lists all the relevant ingredients; and

(d) if the specified warning statement for at least one of the relevant ingredients includes the words ‘in rare cases’—the combined warning statement includes the words ‘in rare cases’ instead of the words ‘in very rare cases’; and

(e) if the specified warning statement for at least one of the relevant ingredients is in the form mentioned in paragraph (a)—the combined warning statement must be in the form mentioned in paragraph (a).

<tr>
<td>751</td>
<td>BACILLUS COAGULANS</td>
<td>A</td>
<td>Only permitted for use in medicines:<br>(a) limited to oral routes of administration; and<br>(b) when the strain of Bacillus coagulans is confirmed to be:<br>(i) Microbial Type Culture Collection (MTCC) accession number 5260; and/or<br>(ii) MTCC accession number 5856.<br>The strain of Bacillus coagulans must be declared on the label.<br>When the strain of Bacillus coagulans is MTCC accession number 5260:<br>(a) the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must not provide more than 6 billion cfu of Bacillus coagulans strain MTCC accession number 5260; and<br>(b) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD2) ‘Not suitable for children’; and<br>- (BACCOAG) 'Bacillus coagulans may affect the way some medicines work, including immunosuppressants. Consult your health professional before taking with other medicines (or words to that effect).'<br>When the strain of Bacillus coagulans is MTCC accession number 5856:<br>(a) the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must not provide more than 2 billion cfu of Bacillus coagulans strain MTCC accession number 5856; and<br>(b) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT) 'Not recommended for use by pregnant and lactating women' (or words to that effect);<br>- (CHILD2) ‘Not suitable for children’; and<br>- (BACCOAG) 'Bacillus coagulans may affect the way some medicines work, including immunosuppressants. Consult your health professional before taking with other medicines (or words to that effect).'</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>752</td>
<td>BACILLUS SUBTILIS</td>
<td>A</td>
<td>Only to be used in a medicine where ADM Australia Pty Ltd (Client ID 33326), who applied to have the ingredient included in this Determination, is the sponsor of the medicine or has given written authorisation to the sponsor of a medicine to include the ingredient in the medicine. This paragraph ceases to be a requirement for this ingredient after 14 June 2026.<br>The route of administration for medicines that contain Bacillus subtilis must be limited to oral.<br>Only permitted for use in medicines when the strain of Bacillus subtilis is confirmed to be Agricultural Research Service Culture Collection (NRRL) accession number B-67989.<br>The strain of Bacillus subtilis must be declared on the label.<br>Bacillus subtilis is not permitted for use in children under the age of 2 years.<br>The maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must not provide more than:<br>(a) 1 billion cfu Bacillus subtilis in individuals aged 2 to 17 years (inclusive); and<br>(b) 5 billion cfu Bacillus subtilis in individuals aged 18 years and above.<br>The following warning statements (or words to the same effect) are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT) 'Not recommended for use by pregnant and lactating women';<br>- (ANTIBI1) ‘To be administered 2-3 hours before or after antibiotics’; and<br>- (IMMUNO2) ‘May not be suitable for someone taking immunomodulators. Consult your health professional before taking with other medicines’.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>753</td>
<td>BACKHOUSIA CITRIODORA</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>The herbal substance must be derived from leaf oil only.<br>Only for use in topical medicines for dermal application.<br>The concentration in the medicine must be no more than 10g/kg or 10g/L or 1%.<br>The medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (IRRIT) 'If irritation develops - discontinue use'<br>- (CHILD3) 'Use in children under 12 years is not recommended'<br>- (PREGNT) 'Not recommended for use by pregnant and lactating women' (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>

<td>A, H</td>
<td>Methyl salicylate is a mandatory component of Betula lenta.<br>Not to be included in medicines for use in the eye or on damaged skin.<br>When used internally, the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 0.001%.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is other than spray, the medicine requires child resistant packaging.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is spray, the medicine does not require child resistant packaging if:<br>- the delivery device is engaged into the container in such a way that prevents it from being readily removed;<br>- direct suction through the delivery device results in delivery of no more than one dosage unit; and<br>- actuation of the spray device is ergonomically difficult for young children to accomplish.<br>The following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (METSAL) ‘Contains methyl salicylate’ (or words to that effect).<br>When for use in topical medicines for dermal application:<br>i) the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 25%;<br>ii) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT2) 'Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant' (or words to that effect);<br>- (CHILD4) 'Do not use [this product/insert name of product] in children 6 years of age or less';<br>- (SENS) 'Application to skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight.' (or words to that effect);<br>- (AVOID) 'Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun' (or words to that effect);<br>iii) if the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine is greater than 1%, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (IRRIT) 'If irritation develops, discontinue use'.</td>

<tr>
<td>927</td>
<td>BORAX</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Boron is a mandatory component of borax.<br>The percentage of boron from borax should be calculated based on the molecular weight of borax.<br>The maximum recommended daily dose must not provide more than 6mg of boron.<br>In preparations for dermal use, which are not for paediatric or antifungal use, the concentration of boron in the medicine must be no more than 3500 mg/kg or 3500 mg/L or 0.35%.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 3 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN12) 'Not to be taken by children under 12 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg boron and up to, and including, 3 mg of boron, and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN2) 'Not to be taken by children under 2 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When for excipient use and the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BORON) 'Contains boron' (or words to that effect).<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BROKEN) 'Use on unbroken skin only' (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>928</td>
<td>BORAX PENTAHYDRATE</td>
<td>A, E</td>
<td>Boron is a mandatory component of borax pentahydrate.<br>The percentage of boron from borax pentahydrate should be calculated based on the molecular weight of borax pentahydrate.<br>The maximum recommended daily dose must not provide more than 6mg of boron from borax pentahydrate.<br>In preparations for dermal use, which are not for paediatric or antifungal use, the concentration of boron in the medicine must not be more than 3500 mg/kg or 3500 g/L or 0.35%.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 3 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN12) 'Not to be taken by children under 12 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg boron and up to, and including, 3 mg of boron, and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN2) 'Not to be taken by children under 2 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When for excipient use and the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BORON) 'Contains boron' (or words to that effect).<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BROKEN) 'Use on unbroken skin only' (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>929</td>
<td>BORIC ACID</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Boron is a mandatory component of boric acid.<br>The percentage of boron from boric acid should be calculated based on the molecular weight of boric acid.<br>The maximum recommended daily dose must not provide more than 6mg of boron.<br>In preparations for dermal use, which are not for paediatric or antifungal use, the concentration of boron in the medicine must not be more than 3500 mg/kg or 3500 mg/L or 0.35%.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 3 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN12) 'Not to be taken by children under 12 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg boron and up to, and including, 3 mg of boron, and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN2) 'Not to be taken by children under 2 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When for excipient use and the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BORON) 'Contains boron' (or words to that effect).<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BROKEN) 'Use on unbroken skin only' (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>

<td>1054</td>
<td>CAFFEINE</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>When used as an excipient, only for use in topical medicines for dermal application.<br>Only for use as an active ingredient for:<br>(a) oral use in adults when the medicine consists principally of one or more designated active ingredients prescribed in Schedule 14 to the Regulations (other than caffeine); and<br>(b) Topical medicines for dermal application that are directed for use in adults only.<br>When for topical application:<br>(a) the concentration of total caffeine in the medicine must not be more than 1%; and<br>(b) the medicine must not be intended for use on broken skin.<br>When for internal use or oral application, the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must provide no more than 100 mg of caffeine from this ingredient.<br>When for internal use or oral application, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When the medicine is packaged for supply as a divided preparation and is for internal use or oral application, the medicine must not contain a concentration of total caffeine greater than 33%.<br>When the medicine is packaged for supply as an undivided preparation and is for internal use or oral application, the medicine must not contain a concentration of total caffeine greater than 1%.<br>When the medicine is for internal use or oral application, a maximum recommended dose of the medicine must not provide more than 100 mg of total caffeine within a 3 hour period.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides greater than 10 mg of total caffeine and the medicine is for internal use or oral application, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (CAFF) 'Contains [state quantity per dosage unit or per mL or per gram of product] total caffeine [per dosage unit or per mL or per gram]. A cup of instant coffee contains approximately 80 mg of caffeine.'<br>- (CAFFPREG) ‘Caffeine intake more than 200 mg per day is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.’<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides greater than 80 mg of total caffeine and the medicines is for internal use or oral application, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (CAFFLMT) 'Limit the use of caffeine-containing products (including tea and coffee) when taking this product.'<br>- (CAFFCYP) ‘Caffeine interacts with enzyme CYP1A2 in the liver. Consult your health professional before taking with other medicines’ (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1055</td>
<td>CAJUPUT OIL</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Cineole is a mandatory component of Cajuput oil.<br>When the concentration in the medicine is more than 25%, the nominal capacity of the container must be no more than 25 mL.<br>When the concentration in the medicine is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 mL, a child resistant closure and restricted flow insert must be fitted on the container.<br>When the concentration in the medicine is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 15 mL, a restricted flow insert must be fitted to the container.<br>When the concentration in the medicine is more than 25%, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or word to that effect)<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25%, the nominal capacity of the container must not be more than 25 mL.<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 mL but no more than 25mL, the medicine must have a child resistant closure and restricted flow insert fitted on the container and the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or word to that effect)<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is no more than 15 mL, the medicine must have the restricted flow insert fitted on the container and the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or word to that effect)<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.</td>
</tr>

<td>Only for use as an active or excipient ingredient for dermal application.<br>When used as an active ingredient, can only be supplied as an uncompounded medicine substance packed for retail sale and must comply with an uncompounded substance monograph of the British Pharmacopoeia, as in force or existing from time to time.</td>

<tr>
<td>1134</td>
<td>CAMELLIA SINENSIS</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Caffeine is a mandatory component of Camellia sinensis.<br>When the medicine is packaged for supply as a divided preparation and is for internal use or oral application, the medicine must not contain a concentration of total caffeine greater than 33%.<br>When for internal use or oral application, the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must provide no more than 400 mg of total caffeine.<br>When the medicine is packaged for supply as an undivided preparation and is for internal use or oral application, the medicine must not contain a concentration of total caffeine greater than 1%.<br>When the medicine is for internal use or oral application, a maximum recommended dose of the medicine must not provide more than 100 mg of total caffeine within a 3 hour period.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides greater than 10 mg of total caffeine and the medicine is for internal use or oral application, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>- (CAFF) 'Contains [state quantity per dosage unit or per mL or per gram of product] total caffeine [per dosage unit or per mL or per gram]. A cup of instant coffee contains approximately 80mg of caffeine.'<br>- (CAFFPREG) ‘Caffeine intake more than 200 mg per day is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.’<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides greater than 80 mg of total caffeine and the medicines is for internal use or oral application, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (CAFFLMT) 'Limit the use of caffeine-containing products (including tea and coffee) when taking this product.'<br>- (CAFFCYP) ‘Caffeine interacts with enzyme CYP1A2 in the liver. Consult your health professional before taking with other medicines’ (or words to that effect).<br>When used in oral medicines, the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (CAMELLIA) 'In rare cases, Camellia sinensis may harm the liver. Stop use and see a doctor if you have yellowing skin/eyes, or unusual: fatigue, nausea, appetite loss, abdominal pain, dark urine, or itching.'; and<br>- (FOOD) ‘To be taken with food.’<br>unless when:<br>(a) the preparation of Camellia sinensis is derived from an aqueous extract and contains 300 mg or less epigallocatechin-3-gallate per maximum recommended daily dose; or<br>(b) Camellia sinensis is used in combination with other permitted ingredients as a flavour proprietary excipient formulation.<br>The total concentration of flavour proprietary excipient formulations containing Camellia sinensis must not be more than 5% of the total medicine.</td>
</tr>

<td>A</td>
<td>Only for use as an active ingredient in sunscreens for dermal application and not to be included in medicines intended for use in the eye.<br>The concentration in the preparation must not be more than 6%.<br>When used in primary sunscreen products, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (AVOID) 'Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun' (or words to this effect); and<br>- (SUNPRO) 'Wear protective clothing - hats and eyewear when exposed to the sun' (or words to this effect).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1139</td>
<td>CAMPHOR OIL BROWN</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Camphor, cineole and safrole are mandatory components of camphor oil brown.<br>In solid and semi solid preparations, the concentration of camphor must not be more than 12.5%.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils, the concentration of camphor must not be more than 2.5%.<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 2.5% but less than or equal to 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect);<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'; and<br>- (BABY4) ‘Do not apply to infants under 12 months of age except on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist’ (or words to that effect).<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 15 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect);<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'; and<br>- (BABY4) ‘Do not apply to infants under 12 months of age except on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist’ (or words to that effect).<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert and child resistant closure fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect);<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'; and<br>- (BABY4) ‘Do not apply to infants under 12 months of age except on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist’ (or words to that effect).<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25%, the nominal capacity of the container must not be more than 25 millilitres.<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a child resistant closure and restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is not more than 15 millilitres, the medicine must have the restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>When for internal use the concentration of safrole in a medicine must not be more than 0.1%.<br>When for topical use the concentration of safrole in a medicine must not be more than 1.0%.<br>If the concentration of camphor is more than 2.5%, the nominal capacity of the container must not be more than 25 millilitres.</td>
</tr>

<td>Camphor and safrole are mandatory components of camphor oil white.<br>In solid and semi solid preparations, the concentration of camphor must not be more than 12.5%.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils, the concentration of camphor must not be more than 2.5%.<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 2.5% but less than or equal to 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect);<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'; and<br>- (BABY4) ‘Do not apply to infants under 12 months of age except on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist’ (or words to that effect).<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 15 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect);<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'; and<br>- (BABY4) ‘Do not apply to infants under 12 months of age except on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist’ (or words to that effect).<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert and child resistant closure fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect);<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'; and<br>- (BABY4) ‘Do not apply to infants under 12 months of age except on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist’ (or words to that effect).<br>When for internal use the concentration of safrole in a medicine must not be more than 0.1%.<br>When for topical use the concentration of safrole in a medicine must not be more than 1.0%.<br>If the concentration of camphor is more than 2.5%, the nominal capacity of the container must not be more than 25 millilitres.</td>

<td>Hydroxyanthracene derivatives calculated as cascaroside A is a mandatory component of cascara dry when the route of administration is oral.<br>When used in oral medicines, if the maximum recommended daily dose contains more than 10 mg of hydroxyanthracene derivatives the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD3) ‘Use in children under 12 years is not recommended’;<br>- (LAX2) ‘Prolonged use may cause serious bowel problems’; and<br>- (LAX3) ‘Do not use when abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting are present, or if you develop diarrhoea. If you are pregnant or breast feeding, seek the advice of a healthcare professional before taking this product' [or words to that effect].<br>When promoted or marketed as a laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statement on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX1) ‘Drink plenty of water' [or words to that effect].<br>When not promoted or marketed as laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX5) ‘This product contains [name of the herb(s) or the chemical component(s)]’; and<br>- (LAX4) ‘This product may have laxative effect’.<br>When used in oral medicines, if the maximum recommended daily dose contains less than 10 mg of hydroxyanthracene derivatives and is promoted or marketed as laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD3) ‘Use in children under 12 years is not recommended’;<br>- (LAX1) ‘Drink plenty of water' [or words to that effect]; and<br>- (LAX2) ‘Prolonged use may cause serious bowel problems’.</td>

If you are pregnant or breast feeding, seek the advice of a healthcare professional before taking this product' (or words to that effect).<br>When promoted or marketed as a laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statement on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX1) ‘Drink plenty of water' (or words to that effect).<br>When not promoted or marketed as laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX5) ‘This product contains [name of the herb(s) or the chemical component(s)]’; and<br>- (LAX4) ‘This product may have laxative effect’.<br>When used in oral medicines, if the maximum recommended daily dose contains less than 10 mg of hydroxyanthracene derivatives and is promoted or marketed as laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD3) ‘Use in children under 12 years is not recommended’;<br>- (LAX1) ‘Drink plenty of water' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (LAX2) ‘Prolonged use may cause serious bowel problems’.</td>

<td>Hydroxyanthracene glycosides calculated as sennoside B is a mandatory component of Cassia fistula when the route of administration is oral.<br>When used in oral medicines, if the maximum recommended daily dose contains more than 10 mg of hydroxyanthracene derivatives the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD3) ‘Use in children under 12 years is not recommended’;<br>- (LAX2) ‘Prolonged use may cause serious bowel problems’; and<br>- (LAX3) ‘Do not use when abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting are present, or if you develop diarrhoea. If you are pregnant or breast feeding, seek the advice of a healthcare professional before taking this product' (or words to that effect).<br>When promoted or marketed as a laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statement on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX1) ‘Drink plenty of water' (or words to that effect).<br>When not promoted or marketed as laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX5) ‘This product contains [name of the herb(s) or the chemical component(s)]’; and<br>- (LAX4) ‘This product may have laxative effect’.<br>When used in oral medicines, if the maximum recommended daily dose contains less than 10 mg of hydroxyanthracene derivatives and is promoted or marketed as laxative, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD3) ‘Use in children under 12 years is not recommended’;<br>- (LAX1) ‘Drink plenty of water' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (LAX2) ‘Prolonged use may cause serious bowel problems’.<br>When Cassia fistula is for use as an excipient:<br>(a) the plant part must be fruit; and<br>(b) must only be included in medicines when in combination with other permitted ingredients as a:<br>(i) flavour proprietary excipient formulation when the plant preparation is an extract; and/or<br>(ii) fragrance proprietary excipient formulation when the plant preparation is an essential oil.<br>The total concentration of flavour proprietary excipient formulations containing Cassia fistula must not be more than 5% of the total medicine.<br>The total concentration of fragrance proprietary excipient formulations containing Cassia fistula must not be more than 1% of the total medicine.</td>

and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils or distillates, when the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a child resistant closure and restricted flow insert fitted on the container.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils or distillates, when the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is no more than 15 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container.<br>When for internal use then the concentration of safrole in a medicine must be no more than 0.1%.<br>When for uses other than internal use, the concentration of safrole in a medicine must be no more than 1.0%.<br>When used as an active ingredient, the concentration of coumarin in the medicine must be no more than 0.001%.</td>

<td>A</td>
<td>Medicines that contain 'deer velvet antler powder' as the therapeutically active ingredient are subject to the following conditions:<br>a) the medicines are for oral use only;<br>b) the antlers (including the velvet) are sourced only from red deer (Cervus elaphus), elk/wapiti (Cervus canadensis), or a crossbreed of these species;<br>c) the deer are sourced only from farmed stock bred and raised in New Zealand;<br>d) the deer are sourced only from herds farmed for food in accordance with the Animal Products Act 1999 (New Zealand) and the regulations made under that Act, as in force or existing from time to time;<br>e) the antlers are removed from the deer only according to the Animal Welfare Act 1999 (New Zealand) and the regulations made under that Act, as in force or existing from time to time.</td>

<tr>
<td>1777</td>
<td>DIBASIC MAGNESIUM PHOSPHATE TRIHYDRATE</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Magnesium is a mandatory component of dibasic magnesium phosphate trihydrate.<br>The percentage of magnesium from dibasic magnesium phosphate trihydrate should be calculated based on the molecular weight of dibasic magnesium phosphate trihydrate.<br>When used in a medicine:<br>(a) with an oral route of administration;<br>(b) not indicated for laxative (or related) use; and<br>(c) where the maximum recommended daily dose for:<br>(i) children aged between 1 and 3 years (inclusive) provides 65 mg or more total magnesium from inorganic magnesium salts;<br>(ii) children aged between 4 and 8 years (inclusive) provides 110 mg or more total magnesium from inorganic magnesium salts; or<br>(iii) individuals aged 9 years or older provides 350 mg or more total magnesium from inorganic magnesium salts;<br>the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX6) 'Contains magnesium, which may have a laxative effect or cause diarrhoea' (or words to that effect).<br>When the route of administration is oral, the medicine must not be directed for use in infants younger than 12 months of age.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1778</td>
<td>DIBASIC POTASSIUM PHOSPHATE</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>When used as an active ingredient and the medicine is intended as a mineral supplementation, potassium is a mandatory component of dibasic potassium phosphate.<br>When used in a solid preparation, the pH of a 10 g/L aqueous solution must not be more than 11.5.<br>When used in a liquid or a semi-solid preparation, the pH of the preparation must not exceed 11.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1779</td>
<td>DIBASIC POTASSIUM PHOSPHATE TRIHYDRATE</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>When used as an active ingredient and the medicine is intended as a mineral supplementation, potassium is a mandatory component of dibasic potassium phosphate trihydrate.<br>When used in a solid preparation, the pH of a 10 g/L aqueous solution must not be more than 11.5.<br>When used in a liquid or a semi-solid preparation, the pH of the preparation must not exceed 11.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1780</td>

<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>When used as an active ingredient and the preparation is intended as a mineral supplementation, sodium is a mandatory component of dibasic sodium phosphate.<br>When used in a solid preparation, the pH of a 10 g/L aqueous solution must not be more than 11.5.<br>When used in a liquid or a semi-solid preparation, the pH of the preparation must not exceed 11.5.</td>

<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Cineole is a mandatory component of Eucalyptus dives.<br>In liquid preparations when the concentration of cineole OR the concentration of oil or distillate in the preparation is more than 25%:<br>a) the nominal capacity of the container must be no more than 25 millilitres;<br>b) a restricted flow insert must be fitted on the container; and<br>c) the container must include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>In liquid preparations, when the concentration of cineole OR the concentration of oil or distillate in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres the medicine must also have a child resistant closure.</td>

<td>FERRIC AMMONIUM CITRATE</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>When for internal use, iron is a mandatory component of ferric ammonium citrate.<br>When for internal use, the medicine must contain a daily dose of no more than 24 mg of iron.<br>If the divided dosage form contains more than 5 mg of iron per dosage unit (excluding up to 10 mg of iron oxide when used as an excipient), the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron.<br>In undivided preparations, the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron (excluding iron oxides when present as an excipient at a quantity of no more than 1%).<br>Divided preparations with a dose of more than 5 mg of elemental iron per dosage unit and more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>Undivided preparations containing more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>When for internal use except for iron-containing multivitamin/mineral products indicated for general nutritional support that do not make specific iron-deficiency related claims, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (IRONDEF) 'Not for the treatment of iron deficiency conditions' (or words to that effect).</td>

<td>Methyl salicylate is a mandatory component of Filipendula ulmaria.<br>Not to be included in medicines for use in the eye or on damaged skin.<br>When used internally, the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 0.001%.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is other than spray, the medicine requires child resistant packaging.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is spray, the medicine does not require child resistant packaging if:<br>- the delivery device is engaged into the container in such a way that prevents it from being readily removed;<br>- direct suction through the delivery device results in delivery of no more than one dosage unit; and<br>- actuation of the spray device is ergonomically difficult for young children to accomplish.<br>The following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (METSAL) 'Contains methyl salicylate' (or words to that effect).<br>When for use in topical medicines for dermal application:<br>i) the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 25%;<br>ii) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT2) 'Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant' (or words to that effect);<br>- (CHILD4) 'Do not use [this product/insert name of product] in children 6 years of age or less';<br>- (SENS) 'Application to skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight.' (or words to that effect);<br>- (AVOID) 'Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun' (or words to that effect);<br>iii) if the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine is greater than 1%, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (IRRIT) 'If irritation develops, discontinue use'.</td>

<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Methyl salicylate is a mandatory component of Gaultheria procumbens.<br>Not to be included in medicines for use in the eye or on damaged skin.<br>When used internally, the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 0.001%.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is other than spray, the medicine requires child resistant packaging.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is spray, the medicine does not require child resistant packaging if:<br>- the delivery device is engaged into the container in such a way that prevents it from being readily removed;<br>- direct suction through the delivery device results in delivery of no more than one dosage unit; and<br>- actuation of the spray device is ergonomically difficult for young children to accomplish.<br>The following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (METSAL) 'Contains methyl salicylate' (or words to that effect).<br>When for use in topical medicines for dermal application:<br>i) the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 25%;<br>ii) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT2) 'Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant' (or words to that effect);<br>- (CHILD4) 'Do not use [this product/insert name of product] in children 6 years of age or less';<br>- (SENS) 'Application to skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight.' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (AVOID) 'Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun' (or words to that effect);<br>iii) if the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine is greater than 1%, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (IRRIT) 'If irritation develops, discontinue use'.</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>2725</td>
<td>IRON</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Only for use in oral medicines.<br>When used as an active ingredient, the medicine must contain a daily dose of no more than 24 mg of iron.<br>If the divided dosage form contains more than 5 mg of iron per dosage unit (excluding up to 10 mg of iron oxide when used as an excipient), the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron.<br>In undivided preparations, the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron (excluding iron oxides when present as an excipient at a quantity of no more than 1%).<br>Divided preparations with a dose of more than 5mg of elemental iron per dosage unit and more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>Undivided preparations containing more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>When for internal use except for iron-containing multivitamin/mineral products indicated for general nutritional support that do not make specific iron-deficiency related claims, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (IRONDEF) 'Not for the treatment of iron deficiency conditions' (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2726</td>
<td>IRON (II) BISGLYCINE SULFATE TRIHYDRATE</td>
<td>A</td>
<td>Only for use in oral medicines.<br>Iron is a mandatory component of iron (II) bisglycine sulfate trihydrate.<br>When for internal use, the medicine must contain a daily dose of no more than 24 mg of iron.<br>If the divided dosage form contains more than 5 mg of iron per dosage unit (excluding up to 10 mg of iron oxide when used as an excipient), the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron.<br>In undivided preparations, the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron (excluding iron oxides when present as an excipient at a quantity of no more than 1%).<br>Divided preparations with a dose of more than 5 mg of elemental iron per dosage unit and more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>When for internal use except for iron-containing multivitamin/mineral products indicated for general nutritional support that do not make specific iron-deficiency related claims, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (IRONDEF) 'Not for the treatment of iron deficiency conditions' (or words to that effect).</td>
</tr>

<td>IRON (II) GLYCINATE</td>
<td>A</td>
<td>Only for use in oral medicines.<br>Iron is a mandatory component of iron (II) glycinate.<br>When for internal use, the medicine must contain a daily dose of no more than 24 mg of iron.<br>If the divided dosage form contains more than 5 mg of iron per dosage unit (excluding up to 10 mg of iron oxide when used as an excipient), the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron.<br>In undivided preparations, the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron (excluding iron oxides when present as an excipient at a quantity of no more than 1%).<br>Divided preparations with a dose of more than 5 mg of elemental iron per dosage unit and more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>When for internal use except for iron-containing multivitamin/mineral products indicated for general nutritional support that do not make specific iron-deficiency related claims, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (IRONDEF) 'Not for the treatment of iron deficiency conditions' (or words to that effect).</td>

<td>Only for use in oral medicines.<br>Iron is a mandatory component of iron (III) glycinate.<br>When for internal use, the medicine must contain a daily dose of no more than 24 mg of iron.<br>If the divided dosage form contains more than 5 mg of iron per dosage unit (excluding up to 10 mg of iron oxide when used as an excipient), the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron.<br>In undivided preparations, the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron (excluding iron oxides when present as an excipient at a quantity of no more than 1%).<br>Divided preparations with a dose of more than 5 mg of elemental iron per dosage unit and more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>Undivided preparations containing more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>When for internal use except for iron-containing multivitamin/mineral products indicated for general nutritional support that do not make specific iron-deficiency related claims, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (IRONDEF) 'Not for the treatment of iron deficiency conditions' (or words to that effect).</td>

<td>IRON AMINO ACID CHELATE</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Only for use in oral medicines.<br>When used internally, iron is a mandatory component of iron amino acid chelate.<br>The concentration of iron in iron amino acid chelate must be no more than 25%.<br>When for internal use, the medicine must contain a daily dose of no more than 24 mg of iron.<br>If the divided dosage form contains more than 5 mg of iron per dosage unit (excluding up to 10 mg of iron oxide when used as an excipient), the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron.<br>In undivided preparations, the primary pack must contain no more than 750 mg of iron (excluding iron oxides when present as an excipient at a quantity of no more than 1%).<br>Divided preparations with a dose of more than 5 mg of elemental iron per dosage unit and more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>Undivided preparations containing more than 250 mg of elemental iron in the total contents of the container are required to have a child resistant closure.<br>When for internal use except for iron-containing multivitamin/mineral products indicated for general nutritional support that do not make specific iron-deficiency related claims, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (IRONDEF) 'Not for the treatment of iron deficiency conditions' (or words to that effect).</td>

<tr>
<td>2859</td>
<td>KALMIA LATIFOLIA</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Beta-arbutin is a mandatory component of Kalmia latifolia.<br>When for oral use, the maximum recommended daily dose must not provide more than 500 mg of beta-arbutin.<br>When for dermal application exclusively to the face:<br>a) the concentration of beta-arbutin in the medicine must not be more than 7%;<br>b) hydroquinone is a mandatory component; and<br>c) the concentration of hydroquinone must not be more than 10 mg/kg or 10 mg/L or 0.001%.<br>When for use other than oral or dermal application exclusively to the face, the concentration of beta-arbutin in the medicine must not be more than 10 mg/kg or 10 mg/L or 0.001%.</td>

<td>A</td>
<td>Magnesium is a mandatory component of magnesium chloride 4.5-hydrate.<br>When used in a medicine:<br>(a) with an oral route of administration;<br>(b) not indicated for laxative (or related) use; and<br>(c) where the maximum recommended daily dose for:<br>(i) children aged between 1 and 3 years (inclusive) provides 65 mg or more total magnesium from inorganic magnesium salts;<br>(ii) children aged between 4 and 8 years (inclusive) provides 110 mg or more total magnesium from inorganic magnesium salts; or<br>(iii) individuals aged 9 years or older provides 350 mg or more total magnesium from inorganic magnesium salts;<br>the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (LAX6) 'Contains magnesium, which may have a laxative effect or cause diarrhoea' (or words to that effect).<br>When the route of administration is oral, the medicine must not be directed for use in infants younger than 12 months of age.</td>

<td>3235</td>
<td>MEADOWSWEET HERB DRY</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Methyl salicylate is a mandatory component of meadowsweet herb dry.<br>Not to be included in medicines for use in the eye or on damaged skin.<br>When used internally, the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 0.001%.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is other than spray, the medicine requires child resistant packaging.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is spray, the medicine does not require child resistant packaging if:<br>- the delivery device is engaged into the container in such a way that prevents it from being readily removed;<br>- direct suction through the delivery device results in delivery of no more than one dosage unit; and<br>- actuation of the spray device is ergonomically difficult for young children to accomplish.<br>The following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (METSAL) 'Contains methyl salicylate' (or words to that effect).<br>When for use in topical medicines for dermal application<br>i) the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 25%<br>ii) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT2) 'Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant' (or words to that effect);<br>- (CHILD4) 'Do not use [this product/insert name of product] in children 6 years of age or less';<br>- (SENS) 'Application to skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight.' (or words to that effect);<br>- (AVOID) 'Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun' (or words to that effect);<br>iii) if the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine is greater than 1%, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (IRRIT) 'If irritation develops, discontinue use'.</td>
</tr>

<td>Until 20 June 2027, Methoxypropylamino cyclohexenylidene ethoxyethylcyanoacetate must only be used in a medicine where:<br>(a) BASF Australia Ltd (Client ID 13479) is the sponsor of the medicine (the primary sponsor); or<br>(b) another person is the sponsor of the medicine (the secondary sponsor) and the TGA has been notified that the secondary sponsor has been authorised by the primary sponsor to use the ingredient in the medicine.<br>Methoxypropylamino cyclohexenylidene ethoxyethylcyanoacetate must:<br>(a) only be used as an active ingredient in sunscreens in topical medicines for dermal application; and<br>(b) not be included in medicines that are intended for use on:<br>(i) the eye; or<br>(ii) broken skin.<br>The total concentration of methoxypropylamino cyclohexenylidene ethoxyethylcyanoacetate the medicine must not be more than 3%.<br>Methoxypropylamino cyclohexenylidene ethoxyethylcyanoacetate must not be used in combination with nitrosating substances.<br>The concentration of nitrosamine in the medicine must be less than 0.000005% or 50 ppb.<br>When used in primary sunscreen products, the following warning statements (or words to the same effect) must be included on the medicine label:<br>- (AVOID) ' Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun.';<br>- (SUNPRO) ' Wear protective clothing - hats and eyewear when exposed to the sun.'.</td>
</tr>

<td>Caffeine is a mandatory component of Paullinia cupana.<br>When the medicine is packaged for supply as a divided preparation and is for internal use or oral application, the medicine must not contain a concentration of total caffeine greater than 33%.<br>When for internal use or oral application, the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must provide no more than 400 mg of total caffeine.<br>When the medicine is packaged for supply as an undivided preparation and is for internal use or oral application, the medicine must not contain a concentration of total caffeine greater than 1%.<br>When the medicine is for internal use or oral application, a maximum recommended dose of the medicine must not provide more than 100 mg of total caffeine within a 3 hour period.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides greater than 10 mg of total caffeine and the medicine is for internal use or oral application, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>- (CAFF) 'Contains [state quantity per dosage unit or per mL or per gram of product] total caffeine [per dosage unit or per mL or per gram]. A cup of instant coffee contains approximately 80mg of caffeine.'<br>- (CAFFPREG) ‘Caffeine intake more than 200 mg per day is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.’<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides greater than 80 mg of total caffeine and the medicines is for internal use or oral application, the following warning statements are required on the label:<br>- (CAFFLMT) 'Limit the use of caffeine-containing products (including tea and coffee) when taking this product.'<br>- (CAFFCYP) ‘Caffeine interacts with enzyme CYP1A2 in the liver. Consult your health professional before taking with other medicines’ (or words to that effect).</td>

<td>Menthol is a mandatory component of peppermint leaf powder.<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application:<br>(i) the medicine must not be intended for use in the eye or on damaged skin;<br>(ii) the medicine must not deliver more than 25% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use;<br>(iii) the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (EYE) Avoid contact with eyes (or words to that effect).<br>(iv) if the medicine delivers more than 1% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use, the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (SKTEST) If you have sensitive skin, test this product on a small area of skin before applying it to a large area;<br>- (IRRIT) If irritation develops, discontinue use.<br>(v) if the medicine delivers more than 5% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>– (MENTH) Contains a high concentration of menthol, which can cause severe skin irritation.<br>When the medicine is for internal use, the maximum recommended daily dose must not contain more than 1 gram of menthol.</td>

<td>Colecalciferol and Vitamin A are mandatory components of Pollack-liver oil.<br>When for use in topical medicines, the concentration of Vitamin A in the medicine must be no more than 1%.<br>When for internal use, the maximum daily dose must be no more than 3000 micrograms of Retinol Equivalents.<br>When preparations for internal use in adults contain more than 33 micrograms of retinol equivalents per dosage unit in divided preparations or per gram of an undivided preparation, the medicine requires the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (VITA2) ‘WARNING: If you are pregnant - or considering becoming pregnant - do not take vitamin A supplements without consulting your doctor or pharmacist [or words to that effect].’ NOTE: Position this warning at the beginning of the directions for use.<br>- (VITA4) ‘WARNING - When taken in excess of 3000 micrograms retinol equivalents - Vitamin A can cause birth defects.’ NOTE: Position this warning at the beginning of the directions for use.<br>- (VITA3) ‘The recommended daily amount of Vitamin A from all sources is 700 micrograms retinol equivalents for women and 900 micrograms retinol equivalents for men.’<br>When for internal use, the maximum recommended daily dose must be no more than 25 micrograms of Vitamin D.</td>
</tr>

<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Camphor and cineole are mandatory components of Rosmarinus officinalis except when the plant preparation is an essential oil or distillate.<br>In solid and semi-solid preparations, the concentration of camphor must not be more than 12.5%.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils or distillates, the concentration of camphor must not be more than 2.5%.<br>When the concentration of cineole in the preparation other than essential oils or distillates is more than 25%, the nominal capacity of the container must not be more than 25 millilitres.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils or distillates, when the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a child resistant closure and restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils or distillates, when the concentration of cineole in the preparation is more than 25% and the nominal capacity of the container is no more than 15 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.</td>
</tr>

<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Where used as an active ingredient:<br>(a) rue oil must only be used as a homoeopathic ingredient;<br>(b) the routes of administration for medicines that contain rue oil must be:<br>(i) topical for dermal use; and<br>(ii) oral;<br>(c) where the homoeopathic potency of the medicine containing rue oil is 12X or lower, the following warning statement must be included on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT3) ‘Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant, or during lactation.’; and<br>(d) where the medicine is for dermal use, the following statement is required on the medicine:<br>- (SENS) ‘Application to skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight’ (or words to that effect).<br>Where used as an excipient ingredient:<br>(a) the route of administration for medicines that contain rue oil must be topical;<br>(b) rue oil must only be included in medicines when combined with other permissible ingredients as a fragrance proprietary excipient formulation;<br>(c) the total concentration of fragrance proprietary excipient formulations containing rue oil must not be more than 1% of the total medicine; and<br>(d) the total concentration of rue oil in the medicine must not be more than 0.15%.</td>

<td>When used as an active ingredient, the medicine may only be for oral rehydration salts in powdered and effervescent tablet dosage forms.<br>Medicines containing sodium bicarbonate for use as oral rehydration therapy are subject to the following conditions:<br>a) the medicine complies with the requirements specified in the British Pharmacopoeia, as in force or existing from time to time, for Oral Rehydration Salts;<br>b) the sodium content and total osmolarity of the solution after it has been prepared according to the instructions on the packet are consistent with the criteria specified by the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the United Nations Childrens Fund (UNICEF) in the document 'Expert consultation on oral rehydration salts formulation 18 July 2001.'<br>c) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (UOAD) 'Use only as directed.'<br>- (DIAR) 'If diarrhoea persists for more than 6 hours in infants under 6 months - 12 hours in children under 3 years - 24 hours in children aged 3-6 years or 48 hours in adults and children over 6 years - seek medical advice (or words to that effect).'<br>- (DIAR3) 'If diarrhoea persists, seek medical advice.'</td>
</tr>

<td>When for oral use, sodium is a mandatory component of sodium calcium edetate.<br>Sodium calcium edetate must only be included in medicines when:<br>(a) the route of administration is limited to topical for dermal use; or<br>(b) in combination with other permitted ingredients as a flavour proprietary excipient formulation.<br>The total concentration of sodium calcium edetate in the medicine must not exceed 0.32%.<br>The total concentration of flavour proprietary excipient formulations containing sodium calcium edetate must not be more than 5% of the total medicine.</td>

<td>A, E</td>
<td>When for use as an excipient ingredient, sodium hyaluronate must only be used in medicines with a topical route of administration for dermal application.<br>When for use as an active ingredient:<br>(a) the molecular mass of sodium hyaluronate must be between 600 and 1600 kilodaltons; and<br>(b) sodium hyaluronate must only be used in medicines when the route of administration is limited to:<br>(i) topical for dermal application; or<br>(ii) oral.<br>When for use in a topical medicine for dermal application the concentration of sodium hyaluronate in the medicine must not exceed 2.0%.<br>When for use as an active ingredient and the route of administration is oral:<br>(a) the maximum recommended daily dose must not provide more than 200 milligrams sodium hyaluronate;<br>(b) the recommended duration of use of the medicine must be limited to three months; and<br>(c) the following warning statements (or words to the same effect) are required on the medicine label :<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only’; and<br>- (PREGNT) ' Not recommended for use by pregnant and lactating women'.</td>

<td>SODIUM PERBORATE</td>
<td>A, H</td>
<td>Boron is a mandatory component of sodium perborate.<br>When for internal use, the maximum recommended daily dose must not provide more than 6 mg of boron.<br>When used in preparations for dermal use, which are not for paediatric or antifungal use, the concentration of boron from all ingredients in the product must not exceed 3500 mg/kg or 3500 mg/L or 0.35%.<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 3 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN12) 'Not to be taken by children under 12 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg boron and up to, and including, 3 mg of boron, and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, one of the following warning statements is required on the label:<br>- (NTAKEN2) 'Not to be taken by children under 2 years old' (or words to that effect); or<br>- (ADULT) 'Adults only' (or words to that effect).<br>When for excipient use and the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine provides more than 1 mg of boron and the medicine is for internal use and/or oral application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BORON) 'Contains boron' (or words to that effect).<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application, the following warning statement is required on the label:<br>- (BROKEN) 'Use on unbroken skin only' (or words to that effect).</td>

<td>SPEARMINT OIL</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Menthol is a mandatory component of spearmint oil.<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application:<br>(i) the medicine must not be intended for use in the eye or on damaged skin;<br>(ii) the medicine must not deliver more than 25% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use;<br>(iii) the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (EYE) Avoid contact with eyes (or words to that effect).<br>(iv) if the medicine delivers more than 1% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use, the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (SKTEST) If you have sensitive skin, test this product on a small area of skin before applying it to a large area;<br>- (IRRIT) If irritation develops, discontinue use.<br>(v) if the medicine delivers more than 5% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>– (MENTH) Contains a high concentration of menthol, which can cause severe skin irritation.<br>When the medicine is for internal use, the maximum recommended daily dose must not contain more than 1 gram of menthol.</td>
</tr>

<td>SPEARMINT OIL TERPENELESS</td>
<td>E</td>
<td>Permitted for use only in combination with other permitted ingredients as a flavour or a fragrance.<br>If used in a flavour the total flavour concentration in a medicine must be no more than 5%.<br>If used in a fragrance the total fragrance concentration in a medicine must be no more 1%.<br>Menthol is a mandatory component of spearmint oil terpeneless.<br>When the medicine is for topical use for dermal application:<br>i) the medicine must not be intended for use in the eye or on damaged skin;<br>ii) the medicine must not deliver more than 25% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use;<br>iii) the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (EYE) Avoid contact with eyes (or words to that effect).<br>iv) if the medicine delivers more than 1% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use, the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (SKTEST) If you have sensitive skin, test this product on a small area of skin before applying it to a large area;<br>- (IRRIT) If irritation develops, discontinue use.<br>v) if the medicine delivers more than 5% total menthol when administered according to the directions for use, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>– (MENTH) Contains a high concentration of menthol, which can cause severe skin irritation.<br>When the medicine is for internal use, the maximum recommended daily dose must not contain more than 1 gram of menthol.</td>

<td>SPIKE LAVENDER OIL</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Camphor is a mandatory component of spike lavender oil.<br>In solid and semi solid preparations, the concentration of camphor must be no more than 12.5%.<br>In liquid preparations other than essential oils, the concentration of camphor must be no more than 2.5%.<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 2.5% but less than or equal to 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is less than 15 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>In essential oil preparations, if the concentration of camphor is more than 10%, and the nominal capacity of the container is more than 15 millilitres but less than or equal to 25 millilitres, the medicine must have a restricted flow insert and child resistant closure fitted on the container and include the following warning statements on the medicine label:<br>- (CHILD) 'Keep out of reach of children' (or words to that effect); and<br>- (NTAKEN) 'Not to be taken'.<br>If the concentration of camphor is more than 2.5%, the nominal capacity of the container must be no more than 25 millilitres.</td>

<td>5217</td>
<td>WINTERGREEN OIL</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>Methyl salicylate is a mandatory component of wintergreen oil.<br>Not to be included in medicines for use in the eye or on damaged skin.<br>When used internally, the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 0.001%.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5% and the dosage form is other than spray, the medicine requires child resistant packaging.<br>When the concentration of methyl salicylate in a liquid preparation is more than 5%, and the dosage form is spray, the medicine does not require child resistant packaging if:<br>- the delivery device is engaged into the container in such a way that prevents it from being readily removed;<br>- direct suction through the delivery device results in delivery of no more than one dosage unit; and<br>- actuation of the spray device is ergonomically difficult for young children to accomplish.<br>The following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (METSAL) 'Contains methyl salicylate' (or words to that effect).<br>When for use in topical medicines for dermal application:<br>i) the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine must not be more than 25%;<br>ii) the following warning statements are required on the medicine label:<br>- (PREGNT2) 'Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant' (or words to that effect);<br>- (CHILD4) 'Do not use [this product/insert name of product] in children 6 years of age or less';<br>- (SENS) 'Application to skin may increase sensitivity to sunlight' (or words to that effect);<br>- (AVOID) 'Avoid prolonged exposure in the sun' (or words to that effect);<br>iii) if the concentration of methyl salicylate in the medicine is greater than 1%, the following warning statement is required on the medicine label:<br>- (IRRIT) 'If irritation develops, discontinue use'.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5218</td>
<td>WITHANIA SOMNIFERA</td>
<td>A, E, H</td>
<td>The medicine requires the following warning statement on the label:<br>- (WITHANIA) 'If you are pregnant, or considering becoming pregnant, do not take without consulting a health professional' (or words to that effect)<br>unless:<br>(a) the plant part is root;<br>(b) the plant preparation is an extract;<br>(c) the extraction solvents are only water, ethanol or methanol; and<br>(d) the maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine contains no more than the equivalent quantity of 12 g dry root.</td>

<td>A, H</td>
<td>Carboxyatractyloside is a mandatory component of Xanthium sibiricum and the concentration of carboxyatractyloside must not be more than 0.35% of Xanthium sibiricum.<br>Atractyloside is a mandatory component of Xanthium sibiricum and the concentration of atractyloside must not be more than 0.3% of Xanthium sibiricum.<br>The route of administration for medicines that contain Xanthium sibiricum must be oral.<br>The plant part must be fruit that is dried, cooked and had the spines removed.<br>The plant preparation must be dry, powder, or extraction preparations with water as the only solvent.<br>The maximum recommended daily dose of the medicine must not exceed 10 g of Xanthium sibiricum.<br>A medicine containing Xanthium sibiricum must not be indicated for use in children, those who are pregnant, likely to become pregnant, or lactating.</td>

## Endnotes

### Endnote 1—About the endnotes

The endnotes provide information about this compilation and the compiled law.

The following endnotes are included in every compilation:

Endnote 1—About the endnotes

Endnote 2—Abbreviation key

Endnote 3—Legislation history

Endnote 4—Amendment history

**Abbreviation key—Endnote 2**

The abbreviation key sets out abbreviations that may be used in the endnotes.

**Legislation history and amendment history—Endnotes 3 and 4**

Amending laws are annotated in the legislation history and amendment history.

The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.

The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.

**Misdescribed amendments**

A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the *Legislation Act 2003*.

If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
